contribution.value: GIFT-SW is a PEFT method that updates only salient weight columns while injecting Gaussian noise into non-salient columns; it also recovers performance of mixed-precision quantized LLMs.

ev.quote: we introduce a novel PEFT method, called Gaussian noise Injected Fine Tuning of Salient Weights (GIFT-SW). Our method updates only salient columns, while injecting Gaussian noise into non-salient ones
we use the TULU-V2-Mix as the main source of data [(Ivison et al., 2023)], as it encompasses a wide range of instructions
we utilize the OpenOrca dataset [(Mukherjee et al., 2023)] to demonstrate that our method does not depend on a specific set of instructions
The sensitivity metrics to find salient columns are estimated based on 512 random sentences from the Pile validation dataset
The Hessian matrix for the GPTQ method is computed on 128 random samples of the Wikitext-2 dataset.

key_results.value: GIFT-SW reaches 73.33 mean accuracy on LLaMA2-7B with TULU-V2-mix, beating FT (71.97), LoRA (71.78) and DoRA (72.03)
At 2-bit quantization GIFT-SW reaches 61.09 on LLaMA2-7B vs STE 58.20 and QUIK+LoRA 41.44 (more than 5 points over second-best)
GIFT-SW matches TULU2 on LLaMA2-7B (73.33 vs 73.49) using 174M trainable params and 500 iters vs 6.7B / 5K (~10x less compute)
Pre-GIFT-SW outperforms at 4-bit (73.15 vs 72.53 Post-GIFT-SW) on LLaMA2-7B but Post-GIFT-SW dominates at 2-bit (61.09 vs 47.08)

strengths.value: Outperforms full FT, LoRA, and DoRA on LLaMA2-7B/13B and LLaMA3-8B with the same training budget across most zero-shot tasks.

ev.quote: GIFT-SW generally shows superior metrics across most models and instruction sets.

strengths.value: At 2-bit quantization GIFT-SW beats STE and QUIK+LoRA by more than 5 points on average accuracy.

ev.quote: In the 2-bit setting, GIFT-SW shows a substantial quality improvement, surpassing the second-ranked model by over 5 points.

strengths.value: Matches or beats TULU2 on LLaMA2 using ~3% of parameters and roughly ten times less compute.

ev.quote: GIFT-SW for LLaMA models achieve comparable accuracy to the corresponding state-of-the-art TÜLU2 models, despite fine-tuning only 3% of the parameters and utilizing ten times less computational resources.

strengths.value: More stable than LoRA/DoRA across data budgets; performance scales smoothly with training data size.

ev.quote: while LoRA and DoRA exhibit unstable performance with scaling data, our method and full fine-tuning are more stable

weaknesses.value: Results reported only on LLaMA models; transfer to other architectures is untested.

ev.quote: We report results of GIFT-SW exclusively for LLaMA models.

weaknesses.value: Only GPTQ (via QUIK) used for quantization; other PTQ methods like RTN or QuantEase not tested.

ev.quote: For quantizing models, we use only the GPTQ method, which is widely used for mixed-precision quantization of LLMs

weaknesses.value: No CUDA kernels provided; lacks an efficient implementation of the algorithm for inference.

ev.quote: we do not provide computationally efficient implementations of CUDA kernels for the algorithm

weaknesses.value: Authors could not confirm models trained with noise injection are more robust to further degradation (Q3).

ev.quote: Q3: We could not confirm that models trained with noise injections are more robust to further degradation.

limitations.value: Method is evaluated only on six zero-shot benchmarks; no generation, long-context, or downstream task evaluation.

ev.quote: We evaluate our method using six distinct benchmarks inherited from various previous studies. In future research, it would be beneficial to include more benchmarks

limitations.value: Sensitivity metric chosen empirically with no clear rule; optimal metric varies by bit-width and model.

ev.quote: the results do not reveal a clear rule for selecting the optimal sensitivity metric, as performance varies across different bitwidths and models with no discernible pattern

limitations.value: Safety, refusal and bias post-quantization are not evaluated; risks acknowledged only in Section 9.

ev.quote: it omits explicit safety training measures, so could be applied to fine-tune LLMs for generating harmful content

limitations.value: Noise distribution fixed to QNI form; alternative noise distributions are not explored.

ev.quote: Noise parameters for fine-tuning the salient weights are determined using the QNI approach. However, other noise distributions may also enhance the fine-tuning process.

future_work_stated.value: Develop CUDA kernels for GIFT-SW based on QUIK and OWQ codebases.

ev.quote: In the future, CUDA kernels for GIFT-SW can be developed based on the code from QUIK [(Ashkboos et al., 2023)] and OWQ

future_work_stated.value: Extend experiments to other LLM architectures beyond LLaMA.

ev.quote: future experiments with different models are necessary

future_work_stated.value: Explore alternative noise distributions for fine-tuning beyond QNI-style Gaussian noise.

ev.quote: other noise distributions may also enhance the fine-tuning process. Identifying the optimal noise distribution is beyond the scope of this paper.

future_work_stated.value: Refine the criterion for selecting salient columns.

ev.quote: This significant finding underscores the need for further research to refine these criteria.
